stock.name: BJ's Restaurants, Inc.
stock.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on six-month return against spy, six-month return against its sector, cash conversion — revenue +3.5% over the trailing year, growth accelerating against the previous quarter, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +2.9%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $50.75 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 121 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 121 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-29.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-10-30) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Trump declares robot imports a national security threat
stories.excerpt: President orders trade talks on foreign-made factory robots, threatens tariffs.
stories.lead:
President Donald Trump has declared the imports of foreign-made factory robots to be a national security threat—ordering new US negotiations with trading partners while holding out the possibility of imposing new tariffs on such robot imports in the future.

Issued on October 28, Trump’s presidential proclamation represents heightened government scrutiny of foreign-made industrial robots that could complicate the manufacturing operations of major US corporations that rely on such robots. Those companies include Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford, electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla, and aerospace and defense giants like Boeing and Lockheed Martin.

stories.title: Quiz: Dictionaries and Arrays: Selecting the Ideal Data Structure
stories.excerpt: Test your understanding of Python dictionaries and arrays, from dict, defaultdict, and ChainMap to lists, typed arrays, and bytearray.
stories.lead:
In this quiz, you’ll test your understanding of Dictionaries and Arrays: Selecting the Ideal Data Structure.

By working through this quiz, you’ll revisit how Python’s built-in dict works, when to reach for specialized mappings like defaultdict and ChainMap, and how lists, tuples, typed arrays, strings, and binary arrays compare when you choose an array type.

The quiz contains 9 questions and there is no time limit. You’ll get 1 point for each correct answer. At the end of the quiz, you’ll receive a total score. The maximum score is 100%. Good luck!

stories.lead:
I’d been writing Python for a couple of years before async programming made sense to me. I understood the general idea, but the syntax just never felt like Python. Why would calling a function with () not run it, and what exactly was I supposed to await?

Eventually I made progress through a long Mentor AI conversation, so that’s how this tutorial works, too. Instead of reading about async Python, you’ll learn it in conversation with your mentor. The interactions show you different ways to use the mentor, and I hope you’ll add learning through conversation to your toolkit.

stories.title: Helicopter carrying six people crashes in northern Indian state
stories.excerpt: The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.
stories.lead:
A search for survivors is under way after a helicopter carrying six people, including five pilgrims, crashed in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand, officials say.

Uttarakhand's Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the helicopter had crashed near a village close to Joshimath in Chamoli district. Rescue teams have been dispatched to the mountainous area, but the condition of those on board remains unclear.

stories.title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam
stories.excerpt: The alleged scheme used stolen identities to claim US student aid, with Kenyans among those charged.
stories.lead:
In May 2024, Francis Mogambi arrived in the United States after winning the Diversity Visa lottery, a programme that gives people from around the world a chance to become permanent residents.

Just over two years later, the Kenyan national found himself at the centre of a US investigation into an alleged nationwide scheme to defraud the federal student aid system.

On 19 October 2026, a grand jury in Nebraska indicted Mogambi on five counts of theft of government money and five counts of aggravated identity theft.

stories.title: 'Affordability? For who?' Voters decide between helping homeowners or public services
stories.excerpt: Candidates across the U.S. have paid lip service to affordability issues. In Florida, the question of how to save voters money, and at what cost, is literally on the ballot.
stories.lead:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. – The ramp was steeper than she expected, but Rachel Dues was not going to stop. Not mere steps away from what she believed to be the most important thing she would do this year.

Dues, 54, gathered herself then pushed hard, propelling the wheelchair that carried her injured niece to the polls.

"You're gonna get in there. I don't care how," Dues said, her voice breathless with effort. She was speaking as much to herself as she was to her niece, 21-year-old Rochelle Covington, who asked to come along to vote.

stories.title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia
stories.excerpt: Video games are good at triggering nostalgia, a key reason why classic games keep getting remade.
stories.lead:
The moment she saw footage from the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Kacey Doran picked up her phone. She had to tell her sister.

Nearly 30 years ago, a 10-year-old Doran had sat in front of her family's TV, reading out the dialogue on screen to her sister, a year younger, as they inched their way through the original Nintendo 64 game's sprawling, puzzle-filled dungeons. Ocarina's fantasy-like story, and beautiful music, enthralled them both.

It was also the first game Doran ever completed. Now, countless memories rushed back to her as she devoured clips of the fully redesigned version, due to arrive on the Switch 2 later this year.

stories.title: Items stolen from Man Utd Munich air disaster memorial
stories.excerpt: Four medals and a crystal trophy were taken from the display, according to German media.
stories.lead:
The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF) has said it was "deeply saddened" after items remembering victims of the 1958 air crash were stolen from a memorial in Germany.

German newspaper Hallo München said pieces were taken from a glass display case at Manchesterplatz in Munich on Monday.

Munich Police told local reporters the case had been smashed with a stone. They believed it to have happened between 08:00 and 13:00 local time.
